content: Vulkan spec guarantees VkPhysicalDeviceLimits::maxPushConstantsSize is at least 128 bytes on every conformant implementation (many implementations support 256+ but 128 is the portable floor) -- confirms D-29's fixed 128-byte threshold is a real, spec-backed, universally-safe constant, not a guess. Push constant blocks in SPIR-V (OpTypeStruct with PushConstant storage class) must be laid out per std430 rules (except array/struct base alignment isn't rounded to 16), NOT std140 -- vec3 members still have a base alignment of 16 bytes (vec4-sized) even though the type itself is 12 bytes, a classic silent-padding trap. Recommendation: restrict push-constant/UBO uniform declarations to vec4/mat4-aligned types (avoid bare vec3/float scalars mixed at arbitrary offsets) to sidestep alignment miscalculation, which is directly relevant to DETV-01 since a host-side struct/GLSL-declaration mismatch causes wrong (but not necessarily crashing) data being read by the shader -- a silent correctness bug that could still be 'deterministic' (always wrong the same way) but wrong.
